validity.recommendation: No action -- existence, classification, and non-duplicate status all confirmed.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: National Fuel Gas Supply Corporation ('Supply Corporation') is a real, FERC-regulated interstate natural gas transmission operator, confirmed independently via National Fuel Gas Company's SEC 10-K filings (FY2020 and FY2025, EDGAR CIK 0000070145), the company's own corporate infrastructure page (nationalfuel.com), and Wikipedia's National Fuel Gas company profile, which names 'National Fuel Gas Supply Corporation' as the operator of the Pipeline and Storage segment. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an operating interstate gas transmission trunk (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission) -- the 10-K describes Supply Corporation's transmission pipeline as moving 'large volumes of gas throughout its service area,' distinct from gathering/distribution lines. DUPLICATE (the row's own SegmentName is 'Main Line' -- this is the parent/whole system trunk, NOT a duplicate of any other roster row): P2537 (FM 100 Project, 31.3 mi, docket CP19-491) is a SEPARATE, specific lateral/loop/extension project (new Line YM58/YM224 Loop/KL Extension) that TAPS INTO this Main Line trunk via the Marvindale/Tamarack compressor stations and the Leidy interconnect in Clinton County, PA -- P2537's own shard (rows/P2537.json) independently reached and recorded this same conclusion from its side (cross_row_leads entry naming P6878 as 'the parent trunk that P6878 records'). P6878 and P2537 are genuinely distinct physical assets (a whole legacy system vs. one 2021-built lateral/loop within it), not a relabel or double-count. No other roster row plausibly overlaps with this system-wide Supply Corp entry.

validity.recommendation: Do not silently overwrite LengthKnown -- the ~1,800 mi Rextag figure and National Fuel's own ~2,200-2,800 mi figures may describe different scopes (the 'Main Line' trunk vs. the full Supply Corporation + Empire Pipeline transmission network including all named lateral/loop projects). Verify whether GEM intends this row to represent only the historic core trunk or the whole Supply Corp transmission system before changing the value; if a Supply-Corp-only (excluding Empire, excluding laterals already tracked as their own PIDs e.g. P2537) mileage figure can be sourced, use it.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's LengthKnown=1,800 mi (sourced to rextag.com, a third-party GIS/pipeline-data vendor, re-verified this pass) is materially lower than THREE figures in National Fuel's own primary disclosures: (1) the corporate infrastructure page states 'we own and safely operate nearly 2,800 miles of interstate natural gas pipelines ... in New York and Pennsylvania'; (2) National Fuel Gas Company's FY2025 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2025) states 'Transmission pipeline represents 35% of this segment's total net investment and includes 2,233 miles of pipeline utilized to move large volumes of gas throughout its service area' (Pipeline and Storage segment, Item 2 Properties); (3) the FY2020 10-K gives the equivalent figure as 2,265 miles -- a stable ~2,200-2,300 mi range across at least five fiscal years. HOWEVER, all three of these figures are for the 'Pipeline and Storage segment' or 'National Fuel' as a whole, which the same 10-K explicitly defines as BOTH National Fuel Gas Supply Corporation AND Empire Pipeline, Inc. combined ('Supply Corporation and Empire provide interstate natural gas transportation services ... through integrated natural gas transmission ... systems'). Empire is a separate National Fuel subsidiary/interstate pipeline (not itself tracked as a roster row in this batch) whose own mileage is not broken out in the filings reviewed. The 10-K/website figures therefore cannot be assumed to describe Supply Corporation's transmission system ALONE, let alone this row's specific 'Main Line' SegmentName as opposed to the many individually-tracked lateral/loop/extension projects built onto it (e.g. P2537 FM100, 31.3 mi, and others outside this batch such as P7827 Tioga Pathway) -- an aggregate system-plus-subsidiary figure is not automatically the correct value for a specific trunk-only segment row (aggregate-vs-segment principle, applied here in the opposite direction: the bigger number may be the wrong scope, not the sheet's smaller one). Per rule 4(e)/rule 7, this is filed as a spec concern with contested left blank (no confidently corrected value) rather than silently replacing 1,800 with 2,233-2,800, and rather than silently passing the disagreement. Recommend a follow-up search of FERC Form 2 (Supply Corporation's own annual report to FERC, filed separately from Empire's) for a Supply-Corp-only system mileage figure, which was not located in this pass (FERC's eLibrary full-text search and Form 2 index were not exhaustively searched for Supply Corporation's Form 2 XBRL/PDF within this session's time budget).

fills.researcher_notes: Confirmed as recorded across two National-Fuel-origin documents (counted as one origin per the independence rule, but both directly and explicitly label this asset class 'transmission').

The 'Main Line' represents a legacy, more-than-century-old accumulated transmission trunk (Supply Corporation traces to the early 1900s Appalachian gas boom) built up over decades from many individually-proposed segments, several of which are separately tracked in GEM under their own ProjectIDs (e.g. P2537 FM100, proposed 2017). No single source states one 'proposal' event or year for the system-wide trunk as a whole -- searched National Fuel's corporate history/about pages (nationalfuel.com/about-national-fuel/company-history/ and /about/ both returned 404), the SEC 10-K FY2020 and FY2025 filings (no system-wide proposal date given), and Wikipedia's National Fuel Gas article (gives only the 1902 PARENT HOLDING COMPANY incorporation date, which per this campaign's addendum rule is a corporate event, not a pipeline ProposalYear/StartYear, and is explicitly not staged as such here). Left UNRESOLVED rather than force an inapplicable date onto a system that was never proposed as a single project.

Same reasoning as Proposal: this is a system-wide trunk built up incrementally over a century-plus, not a single construction project with one start date. No source found states a single construction-commencement year for the 'Main Line' as a whole; individual expansion/lateral projects onto it (FM100, and others outside this batch) each carry their own ConstructionYear on their own PIDs. Searched the same sources listed under Proposal without finding a system-wide figure.

No source gives a single in-service/StartYear1 for the 'Main Line' as a whole -- it is an accumulated system, not a discrete project with one start date. The only date found anywhere near this row's history is National Fuel Gas COMPANY's 1902 incorporation (the parent holding company's founding, per Wikipedia and both 10-Ks), which this campaign's addendum explicitly rules out as a StartYear1 substitute (a corporate-founding event is not a pipeline in-service date). Left UNRESOLVED with this reasoning rather than fabricating a start date from the parent's history.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: National Fuel Gas Company's FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, filed with SEC EDGAR in late 2025) reports the Pipeline and Storage segment -- Supply Corporation's transmission system, this row -- as an actively operating, revenue-generating segment ('contributed net income of $121.0 million in 2025'), with ongoing capital investment and expansion activity described ('Supply Corporation and Empire have completed and continue to pursue expansion projects designed to move anticipated Marcellus and Utica production'). The corporate infrastructure page (undated but current as of this pass) likewise describes the system in the present tense as actively operated. No evidence anywhere in this pass (10-K, corporate site, Wikipedia, Rextag, the routes-repo compressor-station attribute data) suggests idling, sale, abandonment, or conversion. Status=operating is CONFIRMED, newest evidence dated to the FY2025 10-K filing.

cross_row_leads.facts: National Fuel's FY2025 10-K frames Supply Corporation's Marcellus/Utica-sourced gas as moving through the integrated Pipeline and Storage system to on-system and off-system markets (including via the Niagara River/Canada interconnect) -- consistent with, and not contradicting, P2537 FM100's own facility list (a 2021-completed 31.3 mi lateral/loop tying into this Main Line via the Marvindale/Tamarack compressor stations and the Leidy interconnect in Clinton County, PA, per P2537's own shard). Confirms from the P6878 side that the two rows describe a whole trunk system (P6878) and one specific, separately-built lateral project on it (P2537), not duplicate records of the same asset.

summary: P6878 (National Fuel Gas Supply Corporation Gas Pipeline, 'Main Line') confirmed real, correctly classified, and NOT a duplicate of sibling row P2537 (FM100 Project, a distinct 2021-built 31.3 mi lateral tying into this trunk) -- one spec concern flagged (sheet's 1,800 mi vs. National Fuel's own 2,233-2,800 mi combined Supply Corp+Empire figures, likely a scope/subsidiary mismatch rather than an error, contested left blank pending a Supply-Corp-only mileage source). Status reconfirmed operating (FY2025 10-K). UNRESOLVED: Proposal, Construction, Start, Diameter, Pressure, SegmentCost -- no single meaningful figure exists for this century-old accumulated system-wide trunk, each documented with what was searched.
